description: Fig. 13 is a group of secondary-electron SEM micrographs of tensile fracture surfaces of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel. The caption lists five panels, (a) P-70, (b) P-90, (c) P-110, (d) P-130 and (e) P-150, but only panels (b)–(e) were supplied; panel (a) is absent. Every main panel carries a 20 µm scale bar at bottom right. (b) P-90 shows a rough surface with tearing ridges, ductile dimples and a spherical unfused powder particle marked by a black arrow and the printed label "Lack of fusion". (c) P-110 is dominated by ductile dimple rupture, with a yellow arrow and label "Dimple" and a yellow-dashed inset headed "Dimple" at higher magnification with a 2 µm scale bar. (d) P-130 shows a mixed morphology labelled by yellow arrows "Dimple" and "Cleavage". (e) P-150 shows cracks (white arrows, label "Crack") together with "Dimple" and "Cleavage" (yellow arrows) and a yellow-dashed "Cleavage" inset with a 2 µm scale bar. The sequence documents the transition from lack-of-fusion defects at low laser power to dominant ductile dimples at intermediate power and increasing cleavage and cracking at high power.

subfigures.description: SEM fracture surface of P-90 (20 µm scale bar). Rough topography with tearing ridges and dimple-like features; a black arrow labelled "Lack of fusion" points to a spherical unfused powder particle sitting in a cavity.

SEM fracture surface of P-110 (20 µm scale bar) dominated by ductile dimple rupture, labelled "Dimple" with a yellow arrow. A yellow-dashed inset (2 µm scale bar) headed "Dimple" shows the dimples at higher magnification as equiaxed cavities.
SEM fracture surface of P-130 (20 µm scale bar) with a mixed morphology; yellow arrows label "Dimple" (left, pointing to a dimpled region) and "Cleavage" (right, pointing to flat faceted regions).

SEM fracture surface of P-150 (20 µm scale bar) showing cracks indicated by white arrows and the label "Crack", together with "Dimple" and "Cleavage" labelled by yellow arrows. A yellow-dashed inset headed "Cleavage" (2 µm scale bar) shows smooth faceted cleavage facets.

observations.observation: Panel (b), the P-90 fracture surface, is annotated with a black arrow and the printed text "Lack of fusion" pointing at a spherical unfused powder particle embedded in a cavity.
Panel (c), the P-110 fracture surface, is annotated with a yellow arrow and the printed label "Dimple", together with a yellow-dashed higher-magnification inset also headed "Dimple".
Panel (d), the P-130 fracture surface, carries two competing labels in yellow, "Dimple" and "Cleavage", indicating a mixed ductile/brittle fracture morphology.
Panel (e), the P-150 fracture surface, is annotated with white arrows labelled "Crack" plus yellow arrows labelled "Dimple" and "Cleavage", and includes a yellow-dashed inset headed "Cleavage".
All four supplied main panels carry a 20 µm scale bar at the lower right, and the insets in (c) and (e) carry a 2 µm scale bar.
The dimples appear as small equiaxed cavities in the inset of panel (c), while the inset of panel (e) shows relatively smooth flat cleavage facets.
The caption lists five panels (a)–(e) assigned to samples P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150 respectively, but only panels (b)–(e) are present in the supplied image set.
The caption states the images are of the fracture surfaces of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloys; no composition, phase or condition table is shown in the panels themselves.

The citing text states that the P-70 sample exhibited ductile dimple fractures plus fractures caused by decohesion and internal cracks, with poor tensile performance owing to numerous unfused powder particles.
The citing text states that the P-90 and P-110 samples exhibited more-dominant ductile dimple fractures, indicative of superior yield strengths, tensile strengths and ductilities.

The citing text states that internal defects (pores and cracks) and spheroidization phenomena were observed in the P-130 and P-150 samples, leading to low yield and tensile strengths and elongation percentages.

The citing text states that low laser power gives low strength due to unfused powder and high porosity, whereas high power generates stress from high energy density producing more dissociation surfaces and cracks that decrease plasticity.
